answer.rationale: Activation and onboarding completion are both down 4–6% QoQ, indicating degradation in the early user journey. Memory 31 and 86 show that signup simplification and shortened onboarding directly lift activation and time-to-value. Memory 91 confirms activation messaging works, but messaging alone may not address the completion gap. Promotional pricing (memory 73) showed severe retention damage (-12pp) on SMBs and is a risk given competitive pressure; verification will confirm whether that finding holds today. Referral incentives (memory 57) work well for *existing* customers but do not solve the current activation decline. Enterprise sales assist (memory 44) targets a different segment and does not address SMB activation. Simplifying onboarding is the highest-leverage move: it directly addresses both observed declines, has a proven track record, carries no measured retention downside, and works across self-serve segments where the damage is occurring. The experiment will test whether the previous lift holds under current conditions and whether we can recover the 4–6pp loss. Verifying memory 73 ensures we rule out aggressive discounting as a false solution and avoid repeating a costly mistake.
